items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: I used to play with George Shillin when he had... We used to play at the Moose home on Saturday nights

ctx.x: for the Count Van Aachen and the company too. And I didn't know that they were doing it, of course the fellow that was the owner of the store, he used to be around the store at night after it was cold, always come up and see me and I would tell. And he said to me, you know, he said, man, I'm not selling any drums, he said, man, I have a tough time, he said, why don't you come down and sell some drums and some instruments for me, he said, I'll make it worth your while. So I said, okay, I said, I'll do that, I told…
What Shillin is that? George Happy.

That's Happy, not his son. Oh, no, no, well, this is a long time ago. Yeah. And, yeah, I worked there. Yeah, he had, and then of course when Happy, a lot of times Happy Shillin used to get two jobs, and Johnny Lollard, Johnny was the fellow who played the jazz, the hornet, you know, and he also played a little piano, too cool to think. And when he got two jobs, of course this was, if I wasn't working, of course in the daytime I couldn't make them, and picnics and things like that. Well I used to play with the…
